hlni.insight: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
hlni.audienceGap: Students feel overwhelmed by the choice and don't know where to start investigating.
hlni.viewerChange: Encourages students to journal their confusion to form precise questions for advisors.
hlni.support: The observation belongs to this activity and participant; it supports a next question rather than a general prediction.
hlni.payoff: The student realizes they need help with the tool, not a change in degree path, leading to a constructive next question.

reelTitle: B.Com or BBA? The Sticking Point Journal
creativeAngle: Using a personal reflection journal to clarify confusion
objective: Help students move from vague anxiety to a specific, actionable question.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking accessible, supportive guidance, including students worried about marks, confidence, or belonging

shots.name: Stuck in the choice
shots.visual: Two students looking at brochures, looking confused at the table.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA feels impossible. You don't need a guess, you need clarity.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on concerned faces, handheld movement.

shots.name: The logbook method
shots.visual: A hand writes in a journal with two columns: Task and Help Needed.
shots.dialogue: Try a Sticking Point log. Record a task and where you actually get stuck. Example: Task: Analyze annual report. Help needed: Financial formulas.
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Analyze annual report. Help needed: Financial formulas.

shots.name: Reframing the question
shots.visual: Student smiles, pointing at the written question.
shots.dialogue: Now you have a real path. Ask: Where can I find support for advanced financial formula application?
shots.onscreenText: Where can I find support for advanced financial formula application?

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Transforming the abstract choice between degrees into a concrete investigation of specific learning needs.
shootingPriority: The student looking at the question

selected.title: The Sticking Point Journal
selected.audienceGap: Students feel overwhelmed by the choice and don't know where to start investigating.
selected.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
selected.viewerChange: Encourages students to journal their confusion to form precise questions for advisors.
selected.concept: A student sits with a friend, both looking at different course brochures and noting where they feel stuck.
selected.device: Direct-to-camera conversation followed by a quick close-up of a 'Sticking Point' logbook.
selected.support: The observation belongs to this activity and participant; it supports a next question rather than a general prediction.
methodSteps: Try or inspect a clearly illustrative task.
Record one point where you needed help and one question you want to investigate.
Turn the observation into a question for a real course brief or course team.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the recorded observation to choose the next question, not to select a degree from one activity.
selected.visibleProof: A person records a specific sticking point and asks a different, more useful question afterward.
selected.payoff: Use the recorded observation to choose the next question, not to select a degree from one activity.
selected.limitations: A brief exercise does not measure aptitude, learning style, long-term interest or academic performance.

demonstration.input: A logbook showing one column for 'Task' and one for 'Help Needed'.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: Task: Analyze annual report. Help needed: Financial formulas.
demonstration.observation: The student realizes they need help with the tool, not a change in degree path.
demonstration.nextQuestion: Where can I find support for advanced financial formula application?

comparedWith.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
comparedWith.device: A graphic overlay displays a 'Decision Tree' that dead-ends at 'Insufficient Evidence'.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
comparedWith.device: A digital cursor highlighting specific missing grading tags on a screen.

conceptSelection.contrast: Pre-story comparison selected different grounded insights and mechanisms: Trust = insufficient_information / missing_evidence_identification; Connection = task_question_journal / personal_reflection_journaling; Discovery = assessment_questions / tripartite_assessment_audit.
